summary: TLS cipher negotiation regression causes handshake thrash and sustained 5xx error floor
description:
Issue summary: At ~19:05 UTC on 2026-03-10 BrightVoice (enterprise tenant) reported a sustained elevation of 5xx responses and unusually long tail latencies for short chat requests. Impact: ~20% of calls returned 502/503 over a 30-minute window, causing client-side retries and downstream timeouts. Scope: impacts a single enterprise tenant in us-west region during a scheduled model shard rebalance.

Environment: prod-us-west (us-west-2), Redwood hosted inference, API gateway version v2.17.3, serving-runtime v1.9.2, autoscaler v0.8.

Observed behavior: API gateway logs show repeated TLS handshake failures between the gateway and runtime proxies. The gateway enters a backoff loop, reduces concurrent dialing, and many requests fail fast with 502. Simultaneously, runtimes log NVML/gpu watchdog resets and process restarts after short-lived connections are established and torn down repeatedly.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate a tenant warmup: start 200 small streaming sessions to prod-us-west that open TLS connections to runtime and immediately send short prompts.
2) Trigger a model shard rebalance to force ephemeral runtime restarts.
3) Observe handshake failure rate between apigw and runtime proxies and monitor 5xx rate on the tenant route.

Expected: transient retries but no sustained 5xx floor or runtime watchdog resets. Actual: handshake thrash results in sustained 5xx floor and repeated NVML resets on several GPUs.
logs:
apigw: [2026-03-10T19:06:12Z] tls: handshake error: remote error: unknown cipher
serving-runtime: [2026-03-10T19:06:14Z] proxy: short-lived connection established; nvml: watchdog reset triggered
apigw: [2026-03-10T19:07:01Z] backoff: dialing runtime (retrying) count=7 route=brightvoice-usw
serving-runtime: [2026-03-10T19:07:25Z] runtime: signal: SIGABRT (reason: gpu-watchdog)
stack traces and additional logs attached in internal artifact (s3://redwood-logs/sup-908172/).
investigation_notes:
- Initial triage (Aisha): tenant traffic spike coincided with a scheduled shard rebalance; apigw observed TLS errors referencing 'unknown cipher' which is odd since server cipher lists were unchanged.
- Eng (Marco): reproduced locally by forcing mismatched TLS client/server cipher priorities during rapid connection churn; observed repeated older cipher suites being negotiated then rejected by runtime process leading to short connections and GPU watchdog resets.
- Hypothesis: a recent library update in the runtime proxy (PR linked) changed cipher ordering and introduced a regression when connection churn is high, resulting in repeated handshake attempts and CPU/GPU stress.
- Observed autoscaler: concurrent scale-downs were aggressive during rebalance, producing a window where many connection attempts hit a small set of warm runtimes causing connection storms and thrash.
- Cross-ref: Slack #support-incidents thread (https://slack.redwood/support-incidents/CH12345) and PRs above.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Reported elevated 5xx from BrightVoice, opened incident, added on-call SRE.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced handshake errors in staging with cipher reorder; escalated to runtime team and opened PR to revert cipher change.
Leah Ortiz (Runtime) 2026-03-11: Confirmed regression introduced in runtime-proxy v1.9.2 (PR#3421). Preparing hotfix cut for v1.9.3.
Customer (BrightVoice) 2026-03-10: Notified of degradation, asked for ETA on mitigation. Provided recommended temporary limit changes.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Deployed temporary rate-shim for tenant (concurrency cap) and adjusted autoscaler cooldowns; immediate 5xx rate dropped to baseline.
Leah Ortiz (Runtime) 2026-03-12: Hotfix v1.9.3 deployed to prod-us-west; monitoring normalizing.
resolution_summary: Workaround: applied tenant-level concurrency cap and increased autoscaler cooldown to prevent aggressive scale-down during rebalance. Hotfix: reverted cipher-order change in runtime proxy and released v1.9.3. Post-deploy monitoring showed 5xx rate returned to baseline for BrightVoice and no further GPU watchdog resets observed in the window. Customer notified and incident closed.
root_cause: A code regression in serving-runtime proxy changed TLS cipher ordering which, under high connection churn during a model shard rebalance, caused repeated failed negotiations. Aggressive autoscaler scale-down amplified pressure onto fewer runtimes, turning transient handshake failures into a sustained 5xx floor and GPU watchdog resets.
follow_up_tasks:
- Runtime: add CTS (connection-thrash) test to CI that simulates rapid new-connection churn across TLS stacks. (owner: Leah, due 2026-03-20).
- Infra: add a safety floor to autoscaler to avoid aggressive scale-down during tenant warmup and rebalance windows; add telemetry to detect handshake-thrash early. (owner: Marco, due 2026-03-18).
- Observability: add dashboard panel for apigw<->runtime TLS error rate and a paged alert when sustained >5% for 5m. (owner: Observability team, due 2026-03-17).
- Postmortem doc: publish detailed postmortem and remediation steps to Confluence and link to customer support note. (owner: Aisha, due 2026-03-15).
